subject: religious-studies
title: The Quest for the Historical Jesus
welcome_lead: Trace two centuries of scholarly questing from Reimarus to Wright as historians ask who Jesus of Nazareth really was.
meta_desc: A-Level New Testament Studies adventure on the historical Jesus quests, criteria of authenticity, and key figures Schweitzer and Wright.
final_note: You have followed three quests for the historical Jesus and the criteria historians use to weigh the evidence.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hermann Samuel Reimarus's posthumously published Fragments (1774-78) launched the First Quest by distinguishing Jesus's aims from those of the disciples. D. F. Strauss's Life of Jesus (1835) applied mythic interpretation. Albert Schweitzer's The Quest of the Historical Jesus (1906) demolished liberal portraits, presenting Jesus as a thoroughgoing apocalyptic prophet who expected the imminent Kingdom.

Rudolf Bultmann's form-critical work treated the Gospels as kerygmatic confession. His pupil Ernst Kasemann's 1953 lecture 'The Problem of the Historical Jesus' began the New Quest. Gunther Bornkamm's Jesus of Nazareth (1956) offered a chastened historical sketch focusing on Jesus's authority and proclamation of the Kingdom.

E. P. Sanders's Jesus and Judaism (1985) rooted Jesus firmly in Second Temple Judaism, taking the Temple cleansing as a starting point. John P. Meier's multivolume A Marginal Jew applied criteria systematically. N. T. Wright, in Jesus and the Victory of God (1996), argues Jesus reconfigured Israel's story around himself as Messiah enacting return from exile.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.

mcqs.q: How did Hume define a miracle?
options: A violation of the laws of nature by a particular volition of the Deity — and he argued evidence for such violations could never outweigh the uniform experience supporting the laws.
Hume defined a miracle as something amazing or unexpected.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
